correction_note.text: The first snapshot labelled owner() on 21 Ethereum rows NOT_OBSERVED (RPC error; cause not established): rows 6, 9, 11, 14, 15, 18, 24, 27, 29, 32, 34, 38, 40, 42, 46, 52, 55, 56, 59, 61, 67. On these contracts owner() reverts; it was not a provider error. The nightly reader records what the call did, CALL_REVERTED, and names no holder. In this build 21 of the 21 rows read CALL_REVERTED. No other fact in the "What was read" column of these rows was affected. The first snapshot's second-source count on these rows ("6 facts") included owner(), which was not compared; see CORRECTIONS.md.

daily.basis: compared settings at successive producer-declared reads only; intervening changes are not reconstructed
limits: known_at measures evidence knowledge, not an exact on-chain event time.
Equal endpoints and clean daily samples cannot prove continuous control or exact days in force.
A source/failed/partial/deferred/refused/gap state cannot silently inherit an uninterrupted span.

derived_rules.address_shown: the fact's address; "none set" when the fact gives no address and its status word is OBSERVED_EMPTY; "zero address" when the fact gives no address and its status word is RETURNED_ZERO_ADDRESS; UNKNOWN for any other fact without an address
derived_rules.change.last_change: the change records of the daily runs for this row; UNKNOWN when none is recorded (the daily runs compare successive reads only)
derived_rules.counts: counted over the subjects of this view
derived_rules.first_snapshot: the fact with the same field name and the same position among the facts of that name, in the same row (same chain and address) of control-map.json; UNKNOWN when the row or the fact is not there
derived_rules.first_snapshot.same_address: true or false when both facts give an address; UNKNOWN otherwise
derived_rules.second_source.comparison: "not compared (no first-read value)", the published word, when the fact is listed in second_source.facts_not_compared of the row with reason NO_FIRST_READ_VALUE; "compared" otherwise
derived_rules.second_source.fact: control:<field> on Solana, getter:<field> for an Ethereum getter, slot:eip1967_implementation or slot:zos_implementation for the implementation fields, and the admin slot of the same convention for "proxy admin"; "no single compared fact" when none of these names applies or the name is not among the facts the second read reported
derived_rules.second_source.primary_equals_address: for a compared fact, whether the first-read value that the second read compared equals the address of the fact shown (it can belong to an earlier night than the read shown); UNKNOWN for a fact that was not compared

does_not_prove: that a controlling address belongs to anyone in particular
that an authority was or will be used
that nothing outside the readers' declared scope exists
the state after the stated slot or block
that a second source confirmed a fact marked not compared, or any fact of a row marked not sampled

that the label EXIT's row list gives rows 69 to 72 (shown under their names in this page's wording), or an address EXIT's row list names for them, is true: these are EXIT's own statements and were not read from the chain

vocabulary.meaning: the reader found no implementation address in the EIP-1967 or ZeppelinOS storage slots, and the code is not the canonical EIP-1167 clone. Other proxy designs are not read.
the storage slot of the named proxy convention held this address at the block.
the admin slot of the proxy convention was empty at the block; the reader does not read who can upgrade.
vocabulary.word: UNKNOWN (empty admin slot; UUPS designs keep upgrade rights in the implementation)

vocabulary.meaning: the call returned this address at the block. A getter name is not a capability.
vocabulary.shown_in: owner() and, on row 4 (USDC), masterMinter(), pauser(), blacklister(), rescuer()

vocabulary.meaning: the call returned the zero address.
the call reverted. This is what the call did; it names no holder.
the address answered getOwners() and getThreshold(); the threshold and the number of owners are as returned. An interface answer, not proof of a Safe deployment or of who holds any owner key.
getOwners() or getThreshold() reverted, failed with an invalid opcode or returned nothing: the address does not answer as a Safe.
the address held code at the block.

the contract declares the enumerable AccessControl interface and the address is a member of its default admin role at the block; the number is the member count the contract returned (at most four members are read). Other roles, role admins and history are not read.
supportsInterface reverted, failed with an invalid opcode or returned nothing, or the contract does not declare the enumerable AccessControl interface.
the mint account has this field and no address is set in it.
the field held the address shown.
the authority address is a token-program multisig account (reader status supported_multisig); threshold and number of signers are as stored in it. Who holds a signer key is not read.
the authority address is an account owned by the system program. This does not show whether a private key can exist for the address or who controls it.
the authority address is an account owned by a program; its control structure is not read.
no account existed at the authority address when it was read together with the mint.
every fact that was compared was equal at both sources. It says nothing about a fact that was not compared.
the token supply differed between the two slots and no other compared fact did.
at the same block the two providers returned different values for a fact. Recorded, not judged.
a compared fact differed between the two slots: a change in between or a difference between providers; the read does not say which.
no fact of the row could be compared: the second provider gave no usable answer, or the row was not asked because the run had reached its time limit (code RUN_DEADLINE).
no fact of the row could be compared, because the first read observed no address in any of them.
the row has not been drawn for a second read on any night used by this page.

the first read observed no address in this authority field or getter (an authority that is not set, a getter that reverted or returned the zero address), so the second reply is not compared; where there was one, its hash is in the log record and the value is in control-map-nightly.json.
the second provider gave no usable answer for this fact.
the first read observed no address in this fact and the second provider returned one. Shown in full; not judged.
vocabulary.word: second source returned a value the first read did not

vocabulary.meaning: the newest second read of the row belongs to an earlier night than the read shown in the row.
vocabulary.word: an older read than the one in this row

vocabulary.meaning: the newest second read of the row belongs to an earlier night, and a fact it looked at has another value in the read shown in the row. The cell names the fact and prints no verdict; both values are in control-map-nightly.json.
vocabulary.word: second read of <date> compared an earlier value

vocabulary.meaning: the row was drawn that night and no fact of it could be compared; the code in brackets is the job's own.
the second read compared no fact, so it made no log record.
the nightly run has not yet accepted a read of this row.
the read of the build night obtained no answer (the code in brackets is the run's own); the row shows its last accepted read.
the answer of the build night failed the run's own replay check; the row shows its last accepted read.
the read of the build night could not be compared with the read before it and was not accepted; the row shows its last accepted read.
the read of the build night was held back by the run's daily cap on change records; the row shows its last accepted read.
